objective: Implement and locally validate the public/synthetic M1 benchmark corpus, matched-comparison protocol, executable offline fixture checks, canonical event-to-manual-PR-bundle walking skeleton, and the exact local/CI toolchain controls needed to reproduce them, without provisioning the private holdout or performing review, remote CI execution or monitoring, GitHub, merge, or post-merge lifecycle actions.

acceptance_criteria: At least three deterministic, three agent-assisted, and the required blocked scenario classes are represented by licensed public-derived or synthetic fixtures with stable provenance and ground truth.
At least six visible TypeScript consumer fixtures cover direct and wrapper-heavy integration shapes.
The matched generic-agent comparison protocol freezes every control variable and isolates Lumyn orchestration as the treatment.

The offline walking skeleton composes schema-valid M2 contracts from provider event through a manual PR bundle; the deterministic route is agent-free, creates and verifies real deterministic Git baseline and candidate commits, executes the exact candidate head separately from an expected-failing baseline using the authorized npm test --silent command with provider reporting disabled, earns only static_verified, and exercises the fake adapter only in a separate conformance test.
No private holdout content, credential, network request, live Agent Runner/model invocation, GitHub action, or terminal M1 acceptance claim is produced.
stop_conditions: the parent M1 contract or attended implementation packet is incomplete or drifts
a changed path falls outside this implementation packet
private holdout inputs, answers, expected patches, expected labels, raw traces, repository URLs, or plaintext content digests would become visible

review, remote CI execution or monitoring, commit, push, PR, merge, post-merge, live Agent Runner/model, credential, product-command network, consumer-repository, or external-write authority is requested

planning_prerequisite_rule: The planning verifier must regenerate and validate these planning-truth paths before candidate validation; task-executor cannot write them, and validation binds them into the same release candidate.

task-executor.rule: The implementation worker cannot create, edit, or attest its validation-gate evidence.

validation-gate.rule: The trusted validation runner may write only task-run markers, raw logs, reports, and scorecards and cannot mutate the candidate under validation.

scope_exclusions: independent review, remote CI execution or monitoring, Codex review, commit, push, PR, merge, or post-merge lifecycle work
production credentials, network access, consumer repository access, or production mutation
live Agent Runner or model execution
provider access to consumer code or model context
terminal acceptance closure or commercial proof
hosted control plane, provider PKI, connection receipt billing, or annual platform claims
acceptance_checks: Fixture manifests validate provenance, licensing, stable digests, ground truth, expected route, expected edits, expected commands, and expected verification; every agent route coordinates at least two consumer-side fixture files with distinct context-dependent edits and no deterministic recipe.
Deterministic scenarios produce byte-stable candidates and manifests for identical pinned inputs.
Blocked scenarios return needs_input or blocked without speculative edits.
The generic-agent comparison protocol freezes the same repository, evidence, engine route, budgets, tools, commands, role, and verification opportunity for both arms.

The walking skeleton reaches a schema-valid manual PR bundle using only public or synthetic inputs, an agent-free deterministic route, real deterministic Git baseline and candidate commits, exact generated candidate bytes in a fresh read-only view at the verified candidate head, separate expected-failing baseline and passing-candidate processes running the authorized pinned offline npm test --silent command with provider reporting disabled, complete normalized semantic artifact digests, digest-bound package, runner, candidate, fixture, command, output, toolchain and verified-cleanup evidence, static_verified only, and no external write.

Mutation, replay, candidate-substitution, missing/parse/link/top-level baseline failure, isolation, cancellation, scope-escape, live-route, credential, network, and false-verification negative tests fail closed.

coverage_policy_refs.exception_policy: coverage misses block completion without an approved scoped exception and compensating evidence

security_scanner_gates.exception_policy: the attended implementation phase is local-only; scanner and CI evidence remain mandatory before parent M1 lifecycle promotion

engineering_policy_refs.rule: Fixture, manifest, comparison, fake-route, and walking-skeleton behavior stays synchronized with task-readable docs.
Benchmark and skeleton artifacts are versioned, deterministic, provenance-bound contracts.
This phase cannot imply supported distribution, live execution, holdout proof, or shipped M1 completion.

architecture_guidance_refs.rule: Freeze source truth, consumers, feedback, blast radius, and rollback before downstream scoring.
Add the smallest failing M1 fixture, mutation, isolation, or skeleton test before supporting behavior.
This phase remains public/synthetic, offline, credential-free, and network-free; deterministic generation is agent-free and the fake adapter is test-only.

agent_native_cli_checks: Command-facing test output is stable and machine-readable.
Non-interactive failures preserve typed status and evidence refs.
No fake adapter silently falls back to a live executable, model, credential, network, or external-write route.

redaction_posture.redaction_notes: Private holdout inputs, answers, expected patches, expected labels, raw traces, repository URLs, and plaintext content digests are prohibited.
redaction_posture.recursive_policy: reject credentials, secrets, machine-local paths, private repository identity, raw holdout content, and resolving answer material

semantic_invariants: Identical pinned inputs produce byte-stable deterministic candidates and manifests.
Committed artifacts contain no private holdout material or resolving answer data.
The comparison protocol gives both arms the same frozen snapshot, evidence, engine route, budgets, tools, commands, engineer role, and verification opportunity except for Lumyn orchestration.

Deterministic generation invokes no agent; every visible agent-route fixture requires coordinated context-dependent edits across at least two consumer files; the separate fake-adapter conformance route has no credential, network, or external-write authority; and delivery stops at a manual local bundle.

The walking skeleton proves contract composition and trusted synthetic-fixture static verification only; Node vm is not a qualified isolation boundary, and the task cannot claim repo_verified or close runtime, holdout, delivery, real-repository, or commercial acceptance.

changelog_intent.draft_entry: Added the public/synthetic M1 benchmark corpus, matched comparison protocol, executable offline fixture verification, and canonical agent-free walking skeleton.

versioning_impact: Pre-1.0 additive benchmark and test-harness contract with explicit fixture and manifest schema versions.
migration_impact: No existing consumer migration; downstream M3, M4, M6, M7, and M10 consume the public corpus and comparison protocol after parent M1 lifecycle completion.
